selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is one main idea of this passage about the elements and species spread across the earth?
questions.answer: Their wide spread and shared pattern point to one Creator who owns and controls them all.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the reach of the basic materials of creation?
questions.answer: It says they are found all over the earth.

questions.question: What is said about each kind of living thing or created kind on earth?
questions.answer: Each kind is spread broadly across the earth in a united way.

questions.question: What does that worldwide spread prove about the elements and species?
questions.answer: It shows they belong to one Being and come from Him alone.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare elements to obedient workers?
questions.answer: To show that even huge natural forces act under the command of one powerful Lord.

questions.question: Why are species compared to organized soldiers?
questions.answer: Because they are many in number, spread everywhere, and still act under one rule and order.

questions.question: What can we understand about the power of the Creator from these comparisons?
questions.answer: His power is great enough to manage both massive elements and countless living kinds.

questions.question: Does the passage present the world as random or directed with purpose? Explain.
questions.answer: It presents the world as directed with purpose, because the elements and species are shown as serving under one command.

questions.question: What does the phrase about this truth being explained elsewhere tell the reader?
questions.answer: This section is only a short reminder, not the full proof.

questions.question: At the end of the passage, what does the speaker choose to do instead of giving a long explanation?
questions.answer: He gives only a brief indication.

questions.question: Which two big groups in creation are discussed in this passage?
questions.answer: The basic elements of creation and the different species of created things.

questions.question: What is important about the fact that the elements cover the earth?
questions.answer: Their universal presence supports the idea that one Lord oversees the whole earth.

questions.question: What is important about the fact that species are spread across the earth as unified groups?
questions.answer: It shows they follow one pattern and come from one source.

questions.question: How do the individual members of each species support belief in Divine oneness?
questions.answer: Even though they are many, they belong to one kind and point back to one Maker.

questions.question: What is the meaning of saying these things are the property of a single being?
questions.answer: They are under His ownership, authority, and control.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the relationship between the Creator and the natural world?
questions.answer: The natural world serves Him and carries out His command.

questions.question: Why is the Creator described as both unique and powerful?
questions.answer: Because only such a Lord could control all elements and all species across the earth.

questions.question: What lesson about unity comes from the order of creation in this passage?
questions.answer: Many different things can still be governed by one will.

questions.question: Is the focus here mainly on human actions or on signs in creation?
questions.answer: It is mainly on signs in creation.

questions.question: How would you summarize the proof given in this passage in one sentence?
questions.answer: Since the same elements and species are spread across the whole earth in an ordered way, they point to one Creator.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do the elements of creation do in relation to the earth?
questions.answer: They extend throughout it.

questions.question: What does the passage say each species carries?
questions.answer: A sign or mark that points to unity.

questions.question: What idea is suggested by saying a species “conquers” the earth?
questions.answer: It spreads widely and strongly across the earth.

questions.question: Why does the spread of species count as evidence and not just as a fact of nature?
questions.answer: Because their unity and wide distribution suggest one planner and one owner behind them.
